Profile first: data conversion, CPU dispatch, transfers, kernels, and queueing can dominate different workloads. Compilation/fusion removes Python and intermediate-memory overhead; ONNX Runtime or TensorRT can optimize supported graphs; quantization reduces storage or arithmetic cost when kernels support the chosen dtype. Structured pruning removes channels/heads, while distillation trains a smaller model. [1](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/torch.compiler_troubleshooting.html) [4](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531) [5](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00978)

Validate numerical and task-level parity after each step, including dynamic shapes and unusual inputs. Measure cold start separately from steady-state latency. Compilation can incur guards, graph breaks, and recompilation; compressed weights can still require expensive dequantization. TorchScript is a legacy choice in many current PyTorch paths, so follow the supported export/compiler route for the deployed version. Optimize the measured bottleneck, then rerun end-to-end load tests.
